rationale: Verb appears four times in lines 25-27 in a progressive ascent: catechumens → counsel → teaching → thought → mind. Always with ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ ('upward'). Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ϫⲱϣⲧ̄ 'look up' or a specialized verb for upward conveyance through the spiritual hierarchy. Translation 'convey upward' captures the directional-soteriological semantics.
Unattested compound, contextually agricultural (followed by ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruits'). Possible analysis: ⲟⲩⲁϣ ('many, multitude') + verbal element. Tentative.

In tree-typology context, parallel to ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruits' as parts of the tree-body. Possibly related to ⲃⲁ 'palm-frond' or a Lycopolitan plural form. Alternative readings 'eyes' (from ⲃⲁⲗ) or 'released ones' (from ⲃⲱⲗ) less plausible in context.

Lycopolitan variant of ⲟⲩϣⲏ 'night.' The phrase ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲏ 'ship of the night' designates the moon-ship in Manichaean cosmology, paired with ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲛⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'ship of the fire' (sun) earlier in the passage.
Lyc. abstract noun: ⲙⲛⲧ- (state-of) + ⲛⲁⲉ (= ⲛⲁ 'have pity'). Plural with ⲛⲕⲉ- 'other.' Standard Coptic ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁ 'mercy.'
Lycopolitan possessive prefix corresponding to Sahidic ⲡⲉϥ-. Used throughout page 20 in the five-faculty mapping: ⲡⲉϩⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ 'his reflection,' ⲡⲉϩⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ 'his counsel,' etc.
